text: Cures acne in 7 days. Guaranteed clear skin.
rationale: Therapeutic claim on a cosmetic. Reclassifies the product into drug licensing it does not hold.

text: India's #1 Niacinamide serum. The best formula money can buy.
rationale: Ranking and superlative claims with no cited substantiation. Requires published criteria per the ASCI awards guideline.

text: 20% Niacinamide for visibly clearer skin.
rationale: Fabricated concentration: the product is 10%, the ad says 20%. Supplies factsContext, without which POLICY-005 is correctly withheld and this row cannot be tested at all.

text: Your skin is aging faster than you think. Don't wait until it's too late.
rationale: Fear-based framing. Persuasion mechanism is anxiety, not information. Layer 2.

text: Clears leucoderma patches in 30 days.
rationale: Leucoderma is in the D&MR Act 1954 Schedule, so this engages s.3(d) directly. Live exposure for a brightening product line.

text: Fades dark spots permanently. Say goodbye to pigmentation for good.
rationale: Permanence claim, unsubstantiable for a topical cosmetic.

text: 10% Vitamin C + Glutathione Brightening Serum | Glow in 3 Days*
rationale: Real Foxtale copy. Quantified time-bound efficacy claim with no subject count, duration or source. The asterisk is doing work no disclosure follows up on.

text: actively prevents breakouts so you can bid adieu to acne & blemishes for good
rationale: Real Mamaearth copy. Permanence claim.

text: Asia's 1st brand with made safe certified products.
rationale: Real Mamaearth copy. Ranking claim requiring published criteria and an independence undertaking.

text: Nothing else worked on my pimples and marks except this serum
rationale: Real The Derma Co testimonial. Absolute claim in a customer's voice. Layer 2.

text: 93% subjects saw significant reduction in active acne in 4 weeks
rationale: Real Minimalist copy. Quantified claim that carries its subject count and duration. This is what compliant strong copy looks like and it must not be flagged.

text: Reduces Acne, Blackheads & Excessive Oil
rationale: Real Minimalist copy, near-identical to The Derma Co's. The collision that disproves a claim-strength rule. Unquantified, so POLICY-003 does not apply.

text: ~26% more hydration than the benchmark product
rationale: Real Minimalist copy. RELABELLED TWICE, which is itself the finding: this case sits genuinely on the boundary between an unsubstantiated quantified claim (POLICY-003) and a comparative disclosure defect (POLICY-006). It is flagged either way, so the tool catches the brand own copy as intended; only the severity is contestable. Settled at WARN because the underlying study exists and is cited on the live page, making the defect disclosure rather than fabrication.

text: Best used at night, after cleansing.
rationale: Adverbial 'best', not a superlative claim. POLICY-004's matcher must not fire on this.

text: Treats your skin to a lightweight layer of hydration.
rationale: 'Treats' in its non-medical sense. POLICY-001's matcher must not fire on this.

text: 10% Niacinamide. Helps reduce the appearance of blemishes with regular use.
rationale: Hedged, appearance-based, no number attached to the claim, so POLICY-003 does not trigger at all. Minimal pair with seed-007: the only difference is the timeframe.

text: 10% Niacinamide. Helps reduce the appearance of blemishes over 8 weeks of regular use.
rationale: Minimal pair with hn-003. Adding a timeframe makes it a quantified claim, and a bare timeframe is a usage instruction rather than evidence. Tests the exact boundary of POLICY-003 after the circularity fix.

text: Formulated with 2% Salicylic Acid, printed on the front of every pack.
rationale: Correct concentration, checked against real facts. The other direction of seed-003: POLICY-005 must fire on a wrong number and stay silent on a right one.

text: Thoroughly tested by an independent lab and confirmed SPF of 50 was obtained.
rationale: Real Minimalist copy. A quantified claim that names its source. Exactly what POLICY-003 is designed to permit.

text: This serum is good for oily skin and works well under makeup.
rationale: Contains 'good for', adjacent to POLICY-008's 'for good'. Ordering trap for the permanence matcher.

text: Why settle for temporary relief when you can heal chronic cystic flare-ups and eradicate underlying dermal bacterial infections with 2% Salicylic Acid?
rationale: Red-team survivor R1. Therapeutic claim reached by clinical paraphrase and posed as a question. Defeated the lexicon matcher twice over: no listed condition word, and interrogative mood.

text: Formulated with twelve percent pure Ethyl Ascorbic Acid and Fullerene to target dullness and support extracellular collagen integrity.
rationale: Red-team survivor R1. Fabricated concentration written as words rather than digits. The real product is 10%.

text: Standard drugstore sunscreens leave chalky residue and degrade rapidly under heat. Minimalist SPF 50 Sunscreen maintains broad-spectrum stability without white cast.
rationale: Red-team survivor R1. Comparative claim against an unnamed category rather than a named product, so no benchmark keyword appears.

text: Tired of dealing with patchy depigmentation and autoimmune skin conditions? Why not let Minimalist Alpha Arbutin 2% balance melanocyte function across uneven areas?
rationale: Red-team survivor R1. Leucoderma described without being named, and posed as a question. This is the D&MR Schedule exposure the corpus work identified.

text: Minimalist 0.3% Retinol reduces periorbital wrinkle volume by 41% (independent double-blind vehicle-controlled study, n=62, 8-week consumer panel).
rationale: Red-team survivor R1, and the most important row in the set. The study is invented. It passed POLICY-003 precisely because evidence WAS attached. Detail is not evidence, and this is what the registry exists to catch.

text: Minimalist Alpha Arbutin 2% reduced melanin by 70% against 56% for the benchmark, in an in-vitro test on a skin-identical model.
rationale: The counterpart to rt-005 and the rule that stops POLICY-012 becoming a blanket ban on citing evidence. This citation IS in the registry as SUB-005, so POLICY-012 must stay silent. It still WARNs on the unnamed benchmark, which is correct.

text: Apply an even layer twenty minutes before sun exposure. Reapply every two hours.
rationale: Written-out numbers that are usage instructions, not concentrations. POLICY-005 must not fire on written numbers indiscriminately after the rt-002 fix.

text: Formulated with 4 effective UV filters for broad-spectrum protection. Clinically tested to deliver safe daily coverage. Rated N o . 1 sunscreen across Indian retail pharmacies.
rationale: Red-team survivor R2, and the only genuine escape of that run. Ranking claim obfuscated by character spacing. The matcher handles hash-space-1 but not N o . 1, so generalisation moved to model guidance rather than chasing spacing permutations in a regex.

text: One pump is enough. First apply to damp skin, then follow with moisturiser.
rationale: Counterweight to rt-006. Contains one and first in ordinary usage. POLICY-004 guidance must not read ordinal words as ranking claims.
